correctness.rationale: Under independent clocks, conditioning on the switching history gives a centered Gaussian. With r=2D, λ=2k and q=r/λ, excess variance increases at rate r in release and contracts by A=exp(−λC) in confinement. At release starts the stationary solution is the sum r∑_{j≥1} B_{i−j}∏_{ℓ=1}^j A_{i−ℓ}; the L^m norms of its summands are r b_m^(1/m) a_m^(j/m), a summable series for each integer m≥1. This justifies finite moments before using the fixed-point equation H_m=a_m T_m/(1−a_m). The fresh release length is independent of the starting variance, and conditioning on occupation in release gives age measure P(B>z) dz/b_1. Integrating the powers of U+rz gives (2), correctly normalized by b_1. Gaussian even-moment division and binomial centering recover F_m from the observed law; odd moments vanish. For known B, the coefficient of H_m in (2) is one, and T_m contains a positive j=0 term, so a_m=H_m/(H_m+T_m) is uniquely recovered. Hausdorff determinacy and injectivity of C↦exp(−λC) then identify C. For known C and b_1, (1) gives H_m before (2) recovers b_{m+1} at positive coefficient r^m/[(m+1)b_1]; identifying the law of B uses its stated moment determinacy. With B and coefficients held fixed, equality of the first K even spatial moments is equivalent to equality of the first K exponential moments of C. At K+3 positive distinct durations, perturb positive weights in a nonzero kernel annihilating mass, mean and those K moments. For arbitrary calibrated coefficients the same construction uses c_j=j log(2)/λ. For the lower bound substitute z=exp(−λc): a combination of the K+2 functions is a polynomial of degree ≤K plus a multiple of log z. If that multiple is nonzero, derivative K+1 never vanishes, giving at most K+1 distinct zeros by Rolle; otherwise the polynomial bound applies. Thus the evaluation matrix on any K+2 distinct points is nonsingular, and signed differences on that many or fewer points cannot match all measurements. An independent exact-rational replay at K=1 with B=1 and r=λ=q=1 gave a_1=15/64 for both clocks, a_2=13/160 and 217/2560, common E[X²|release]=177/98 and fourth moments 24449/2401 and 390461/38269. Replay the numbers by summing a_m=∑p_j 2^(−mj) for p=(9/40,7/20,1/8,3/10) or (11/40,3/20,3/8,1/5), using H_1=a_1/(1−a_1), H_2=a_2(1+2H_1)/(1−a_2), F_1=H_1+1/2, F_2=H_2+H_1+1/3. The simulation's asserted tolerance is 0.025, not a certificate of the prose's reported error below 0.003. Neither reporting point is used in the all-order proof. No noisy inversion or identification of both unknown clocks is established.

value.rationale: This distinguishes what can actually be identified with one temporally calibrated clock from what cannot be identified by any fixed finite list of even moments, even with a second mean constraint. The exact minimal combined support K+3 is a scientifically interpretable sharp data limit, useful when comparing finite plausible duration laws. The result is an identifiability statement rather than an unsupported claim of experimental stability.
